requirements.name: Phased-array / beamforming signal processing

lines.quote: I designed and implemented a 32-channel acoustic beamformer for an industrial noise-source localisation product. The system used delay-and-sum and MVDR beamforming on an ARM Cortex-A platform, with real-time processing of all 32 channels at 48 kHz sample rate.

requirements.note: The described beamforming work is on an acoustic/microphone array rather than an RF phased array; the candidate's own letter notes the domain difference ('The physics is different from radar — acoustic wavelengths, no RF front end'). Whether this satisfies the requirement's RF/radar/sonar/comms-array framing is a judgement call for the recruiter.

lines.quote: Embedded DSP in C/C++: designed and implemented real-time signal processing pipelines on ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-A platforms for Tuulikallio's sensor product range, including fixed-point DSP kernels, DMA management, and bare-metal scheduling under hard real-time constraints

Developed and maintained the Python-based data analysis and visualisation framework (~18k LOC, pytest, CI-integrated) used by Tuulikallio's application engineering team for on-site commissioning and calibration of deployed sensor arrays.
I am also familiar with Kalman filtering and state estimation techniques, which I understand are relevant to the tracking and platform-compensation aspects of your instrument designs.
Led the three-person software team during the framework's development. Responsible for architecture decisions, code review, and integration with the embedded firmware layer.
All work performed under standard EU free-movement rights as a Swedish-Italian dual national.
I live in Oulu, I have been here since 2009, and I am not looking to leave the city.

ask_in_screening.question: Can you describe any hands-on RF test-bench experience you have, such as with network analysers, spectrum analysers, or anechoic-chamber measurement?
